# What gets indexed, and by which rung

There is one ingest path and it is the task queue. A document's tasks are not a fixed
sequence: each rung below declares the conditions under which it applies, and the planner
reads those declarations. Adding a rung means registering a handler, not editing a ladder
of conditionals.

## The rungs

*Requires* must all hold; *does not run when* is a disjunction of exclusions. A name
beginning `@` is a per-format sentinel — it resolves to whichever pattern that format uses
to make the claim, and a format with no entry makes the requirement unsatisfiable rather
than false. A pattern nothing measures leaves the rung standing down with that as its
stated reason.

*Runs on* is the rung's scope. A rung scoped to nodes another rung produced is not
evaluated when the file is first probed — those nodes do not exist yet — and is asked for
at the moment they do.

| task | runs on | writes | requires | does not run when | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `extract:text` | the file node | `self` | `has_text_layer` | `is_damaged = True` | — |
| `ocr` | the file node | nothing (always skipped) | `is_scanned` | — | — |
| `structure:declared` | the file node | `children` | `has_text_layer`, `@declared_structure` | `@conversation` | `extract:text` |
| `structure:inferred` | the file node | `children` | `has_text_layer` | `@declared_structure`, `@conversation` | `extract:text` |
| `structure:conversation` | the file node | `children` | `has_text_layer`, `@conversation` | — | `extract:text` |
| `structure:sheets` | the file node | `children` | `@sheet_list` | — | — |
| `profile:sheet` | `children` nodes produced by `structure:sheets`, usetype `sheet` | `children` | `@sheet_list` | — | — |
| `extract:sheet` | `children` nodes produced by `structure:sheets`, usetype `sheet` | `children` | `@sheet_list` | — | `profile:sheet` |
| `extract:tables` | the file node | `children` | `has_text_layer`, `pages_with_tables` | — | `extract:text` |
| `extract:images` | the file node | `children` | `has_images` | — | — |
| `citation` | the file node | `subtree` | `@page_geometry` | — | `structure:declared`, `structure:inferred` |
| `index:bm25` | the file node | `self` | `has_text_layer` | — | `structure:declared`, `structure:inferred`, `structure:conversation` |
| `extract:facts` | the file node | `self` | `options.facts.enabled`, `has_text_layer` | `char_count < options.facts.min_characters` | `structure:declared`, `structure:inferred`, `structure:conversation` |
| `embed` | `children` nodes produced by `structure:declared`, `structure:inferred`, `structure:conversation`, `profile:sheet`, `extract:sheet`, usetype `chunk`, `record`, `profile`, `cell`, `table` | `self` | — | — | — |

## What each task reads and writes

A locus separates the node a task reads from the node it writes: `self` is the node the
task runs on, `children` and `subtree` are the regions below it, and `ancestor` is a read
of the node above (legal only as a read).

| task | reads | writes | cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `citation` | `extraction@self`, `text@self`, `blob@self`, `source_span@subtree` | `source_anchor@subtree` | `cpu` |
| `derive:rule` | — | `text@self` | `cpu` |
| `embed` | `text@self` | `embedding@self` | `model` |
| `extract:facts` | `text@self`, `text@subtree` | — | `llm` |
| `extract:sheet` | `sheet@self`, `sheet.measurements@self`, `blob@ancestor` | `sheet.shape@self`, `text@subtree`, `record@children`, `cell@subtree`, `table@children` | `cpu` |
| `extract:text` | `matched@self`, `blob@self` | `text@self`, `extraction@self` | `cpu` |
| `fetch:arxiv` | `source@self` | `blob@self`, `file@self` | `cpu` |
| `fetch:path` | `source@self` | `blob@self`, `file@self` | `cpu` |
| `fetch:url` | `source@self` | `blob@self`, `file@self` | `cpu` |
| `index:bm25` | `text@self`, `text@subtree` | — | `cpu` |
| `probe` | `file@self`, `blob@self` | `matched@self` | `cpu` |
| `profile:sheet` | `sheet@self`, `blob@ancestor` | `sheet.measurements@self`, `profile@children`, `text@children` | `cpu` |
| `structure:conversation` | `matched@self`, `blob@self`, `text@self` | `structure@self`, `structure@subtree`, `text@subtree` | `cpu` |
| `structure:declared` | `text@self`, `extraction@self`, `matched@self` | `structure@self`, `structure@subtree`, `text@subtree`, `source_span@subtree` | `cpu` |
| `structure:inferred` | `text@self`, `extraction@self`, `matched@self` | `structure@self`, `structure@subtree`, `text@subtree`, `source_span@subtree` | `cpu` |
| `structure:semantic` | `embedding@children`, `text@children` | `structure@children` | `cpu` |
| `structure:sheets` | `matched@self`, `blob@self` | `structure@self`, `sheet@children` | `cpu` |
| `summarize` | `text@children` | `effective_content@self`, `embedding@self` | `model` |
| `summarize:llm` | `text@children` | `effective_content@self`, `embedding@self` | `llm` |

| `validate:shape` | — | `text@self` | `cpu` |

## Handlers with no row

Registered task types that the table above does not plan, because something other than the
per-document planner asks for them: the upload path enqueues `probe` and whichever
`fetch:*` the entry point names, the settling walk asks for the rollups, and the rest are
operations a caller invokes directly.

`derive:rule`, `fetch:arxiv`, `fetch:path`, `fetch:url`, `probe`, `structure:semantic`, `summarize`, `summarize:llm`, `summarize:tree`, `validate:shape`

## Retrieval visibility

A document carries a `settled` state and the retrieval indexes are partial on it, so a
node whose tasks are still running is invisible to search until the settling walk
completes it. That is why a freshly uploaded file returns nothing and then returns
everything, rather than returning half a tree.
